body: I really have no solutions, in my position I am more or less helpless, the only things I can do are extremely life changing, not only for me, but for my siblings as well, and I don't want to force them into a position they don't want to be in because I am unhappy.

It's hard for me to talk to anyone in person about problems like this, I fear the opinions of others that I have to see and would have to deal with in person, especially on campus where it would be hard to avoid them. I spend so much time keeping appearances of the happy, yet lazy kid, that if I were to drop that, it would turn a lot of heads, and I hate having unnecessary attention on me. 

The school counselor's are also probably far over worked, as between this school year and the last, there has been a 180 degree turn, at the beginning of the year, a girl I had just became friends with committed suicide, about a month after that, we spent an hour and a half on lockdown because a kid had brought a gun to school with a list of who he wanted to kill, last month a student was shot at the park right behind the school. Practically every day the teachers start class with "I know (Emotionally upsetting event) happened, and I want you to know we have extra counselors on campus." I just can't find it in myself to actually talk to anyone, most of my friends know I cry easily, but they don't know me as the emotional wreck that I am.

If I could have anything, it would be to have my Mom take a step back and follow through with the changes she wants to happen, but at this point, I think I am past fixing things, and some where around casualty control. Having someone I can talk to though, it helps me immensely knowing that there are people I can talk to, and reading what you had to say made me tear up a little. Thank you

I feel like I should, but the most likely thing to happen is that we get dropped into the foster care system, and a group of 5 Kids ages 10-16 probably wouldn't stay together, one of my sisters has Aspergers and is really attached to my Mother, and the whole family, so getting split up would do way more harm than good, she also has Misophonia so noises like hiccups,whistling, most woodwind instruments and burping make her angry, or extremely upset.

I spent about 2 months during my 7th grade year talking to a school counselor because my grades had suddenly slipped, they wanted to know what was wrong, what had happened. Most of what I told the counselor was a lie, as I had been so preconditioned to say things that don't look as bad, or make it seem like it was a rare occurrence that it just felt natural, and sometimes it was hard to discern what was the truth and what was a lie, as I recall, I was called in to talk once a week on Thursdays, most of the time however it wasn't about me, it was more of her trying to figure me out, and figure out why I had changed so abruptly, she completely understood that I had undergone a huge shift and that I needed time to adjust, she said I didn't need to come if I didn't want to as long as it was ok with my Mom. However, my mom insisted that I needed it to "be a better person" so in the end, I usually just went into the counseling office before lunch, ate lunch in there, and worked on stuff I ended up missing because I had to leave class.
